key_insights: NDX fell 5.5% on Nov 5, 2026, its worst daily move since March 2020, after a challenging October. The desk says the post-midterm reprieve faded before the index dropped back below a key level.

US-listed ETFs traded $580 billion notional on Nov 5, the third largest day in the desk's dataset, and made up 33% of total market volume versus a 28% average. On the morning of Nov 6, ETFs were 36% of volume, with dollar volume running +65% above the 20-day average.

QQQ set a notional volume record of $86 billion. Levered semiconductor ETFs (SOXL/SOXS) printed over $37 billion combined, with both setting records. EWT (Taiwan) traded $2.2 billion, MAGS (Mag7) traded $890 million (a record), and XLV had its busiest session in over a year at $4.6 billion.

Net flows across levered and inverse ETFs were +$1.1 billion on Nov 5. Levered ETFs took in +$3.3 billion and inverse ETFs lost $2.2 billion, the widest gap between the two groups in the desk's dataset. Both figures are records.
Levered ETF flows have historically been strongest on -2σ market days and weakest on +2σ days, which is consistent with Nov 5 flows.
Levered and inverse ETF AUM is just under $140 billion, down $55 billion over 20 days. Gross exposure (AUM times the absolute leverage ratio) is down $135 billion over the same period.
Several six-month lows were set on Nov 5, many with their worst session since 2020: NDX, SMH/SOXX (semis), EWY (Korea), IWF (growth) and MTUM (momentum).

Defensive rotation continues. XLU is on track to beat SPX for a sixth straight week, the longest streak since 2022. USMV (minimum volatility) versus SPX is tracking the same. XLV has taken in over $1.5 billion in two weeks, the largest 9-day haul since 2022. XRT had its best week of inflows since May (+$200mm) after an all-time high earlier in the week. XLP is just below its all-time high.
